## Project Goals
 

- <span style="color:orange">**Primary:**</span> To map winter wolverine distributions across the western U.S. to track changes in occurence over time (i.e., contraction or expansion)

. . .

- <span style="color:orange">**Secondary:**</span> To understand the factors that govern wolverine occurence in the western United States.


## Modeling Option 1

<span style="color:orange">**Naive Occupancy:**

</span> $\hat{\psi} = \frac{\sum y_i}{n}$, $y \in \{0,1\}$ 

## Modeling Option 2

<span style="color:orange">**Fit occupancy model with covariates:**</span> 

$$
\begin{align*}
\textbf{y}_{i} \sim& \text{Binomial}(z_i\times p_{i}, J)\\
z_i \sim& \text{Bernoulli}(\psi_i)\\
\text{logit}(\psi_{i}) =& \alpha_0 + \alpha_1 \times \text{human.mod}_{i} + \\ &\alpha_2 \times \text{elev}_{i} +  \alpha_3 \times \text{snow.depth}_{i} \\
\text{logit}(p_{i}) =& \beta_0  \\
\end{align*}
$$

## Modeling Option 2a {.scrollable}

<span style="color:orange">**Predict occupancy for the whole sampling frame**</span> . I.e., prediction with covariates.

. . .

![](/img//wolverine_covs.png){fig-align="center" width=120% .nostretch}

## Modeling Option 2b

<span style="color:orange">**Predict occupancy only at sampled sites**</span> 

![](/img//wafwa_2017_dets.png){fig-align="center"  width=70% .nostretch}


## Modeling Option 3

<span style="color:orange">**Multi-model comparison; predict occupancy at the whole sampling frame or only sampled sites**</span> 

```{r,echo=FALSE}
aic.tab=data.frame(model=c("psi ~ 1",
                           "psi ~ human.mod",
                           "psi ~ elev",
                           "psi ~ snow.depth",
                           "psi ~ human.mod + elev + snow.depth"
                           ),
                   AIC=c(rep("",5)),
                   DeltaAIC=c(rep("",5)),
                   AIC.Weights=c(rep("",5))
                   
                   )
knitr::kable(aic.tab)
```

## Modeling Option 4a {.scrollable}

<span style="color:orange">**Predictions from a spatial occupancy model at the whole sampling frame**</span>. For example, intrinsic conditional autoregressive model (ICAR). 

- covariates are not needed
- leverages 'closeness' of the detection data to estimate occupancy


. . .

![](/img//spatial_occ_map.png){fig-align="center" width=80% .nostretch}



## Modeling Option 4b {.scrollable}

<span style="color:orange">**Predictions from a spatial occupancy model WITH COVARIATES at the whole sampling frame**</span>. 

- can add covariates on detection or occupancy
- the spatial process and spatial covariates are not necessarily uniquely identifiable (inference may be unclear)


## Modeling Option 5

<span style="color:orange">**Prediction from a non-linear supervised machine learning algorithm at the whole sampling frame**</span>. For example, 'random forests', 'gradient boosting', 'maximum entropy'.

- covariates required
- non-linear relationships are handled
- correlation among variables is fine
- trains model based on cross validation

## Options Summary

1) <span style="color:orange">Naive occupancy</span>
2) <span style="color:orange">Single occupancy model</span>, predict --> sampling frame OR sampled sites
3) <span style="color:orange">Multi-model occupancy approach</span>, predict --> sampling frame OR sampled sites
4) <span style="color:orange">Single spatial occupancy model</span>. No covariates or with covariates. Predict --> sampling frame
5) <span style="color:orange">Non-linear supervised machine learning algorithm</span>. Predict --> sampling frame
